chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Muadhi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi al-Hamadani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fuddal narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rida Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them both).

He (AS) said: I asked him about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Allah made them subject' [9:79], and about His Word: 'Allah mocks them' [2:15], and about His Word: 'And they planned, and Allah planned' [8:30], and about His Word: 'They strive to deceive Allah, and He is deceiving them' [4:142]. So he (AS) said: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, does not scoff, nor mock, nor plan, nor deceive. Rather, He, the Mighty and High, will punish them with the recompense of scoffing, the recompense of mockery, the recompense of planning, and the recompense of deception. Exalted is Allah, the Elevated and Great, from what the unjust say.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the Quran says Allah 'mocks' or 'plans'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that divine attributes like mockery and deception in the Quran are metaphorical, signifying that Allah repays disbelievers with a recompense equivalent to their own actions rather than literally performing human gestures. This explanation aligns with the Shia theological principle of *tanzih* (divine transcendence), ensuring that Allah is free from the imperfections (*naqs*) and physical limitations attributed to created beings, as affirmed by the verse 'Exalted is Allah above what they say.'

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 1. Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Yunu

s al-Mu`adhi said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa`id al-Kufi al-Hamadani said: `Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn `Ali ibn Fuddal on the authority of his father that I asked `Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (AS) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: "Allah will pay them back their scoffing," [9:79] and about His Word: "Allah shall pay them back their mockery," [2:15] and about His Word: "And they planned and Allah (also) planned," [8:30] and about His Word: "They strive to deceive Allah, and He shall requite their deceit to them." [4:142] Consequently, he (AS) replied, “Verily, Allah, the Blessed, does not scoff, mock, plan or deceive. However, He, the Mighty and High, will punish them for scoffing, mockery, planning, and deception. Exalted is Allah, the Elevated, and the Great, from the words of the unjust.”
